messages:
sara liu: Heads up — bringing up tungsten-9b (int4) on canary yesterday. Baseline fp16 looked fine but int4 has ~15% higher p95 latency and a small QA regression on our 'closed-book' eval set. Can we triage?

matt choi: can you paste the perf numbers and the eval diffs?

sara liu: p50: 82ms -> 95ms, p95: 340ms -> 390ms, tokens/s down ~12%. Eval: F1 on QA down 2.3 points (mainly longer answers hallucinating).

jin park: did you use per-channel quant or symmetric int4?

sara liu: used symmetric int4 w/ block size 128, default quant script from model-ingest. No per-layer overrides.

aman singh: likely two things: kernel launch overhead + KV cache behavior. Int4 reduces compute but increases memory pressure on KV-> fragmentation. Any OOMs?

sara liu: no OOMs, but heap fragmentation spikes in logs around long-generation traces. Posting snippet:```
[2026-03-19 22:11:03] mem: total=32G used=27.8G free=4.2G frag=1.9G
[2026-03-19 22:11:04] gc: kv_warmup=0.8s prefetch=0.12s
```

matt choi: try lowering max_batch_size and increase batch_timeout slightly for int4. Also reduce default max_new_tokens for this model to 128 (was 256) while we debug.

jin park: agreed. If fragmentation is high, smaller batches help. Also check allocator flags — we saw improvement with `MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=2` on similar rigs.

aman singh: config suggestion:```
model_config {
  name: "tungsten-9b-int4"
  max_batch_size: 6
  batch_timeout_ms: 12
  max_new_tokens_default: 128
  kv_prefetch: true
  kv_eviction_policy: "lru" 
}
```

sara liu: running that now on canary. matt, can you spin a small eval job (1000 samples) to compare quality w/ new defaults vs fp16 baseline? Use same prompts and seed.

matt choi: on it. command: `./bench/run_eval --model tungsten-9b-int4 --cfg canary-tune.json --seed 42 --samples 1000`

bench-bot: eval queued (job 8729). ETA ~8m.

ci-bot: note: canary deploy triggered for shard s-04. Watch for spillover requests.

jin park: another axis — quantization per-layer: try keeping first 4 layers float16 or int8 hybrid. Our last regression on a different model was concentrated in early layers. Could reduce hallucination.

sara liu: good idea. I'll run a small per-layer quant sweep today: float16 for layers 0-3, int4 elsewhere.

matt choi: if latency still bad, instrument kernel times (attention, matmul) with nvprof-lite. Might be that int4 kernels use slower emulation path for some ops.

bench-bot: job 8729 finished. Results: int4 (config above) vs fp16 baseline: p95 delta improved to +6% (was +15%), F1 regression reduced to -0.6 pts. Full logs: /rds/bench/8729/artifacts.tar.gz

sara liu: that's promising. So smaller batch + lower max_new_tokens helped a lot. Plan: keep these defaults, run per-layer quant sweep and kernel profiling. If per-layer hybrid fixes remaining regression, we'll promote.

aman singh: also add a temporary rollout rule to limit concurrency on this model in Dedicated to avoid spike-induced fragmentation.

jin park: I'll add an automated eval check (quality gate) to the canary pipeline to block promotion if F1 drops >1 pt.

sara liu: thanks. I'll file a quick follow-up with the exact per-layer configs and bench artifacts.

matt choi: TL;DR: int4 gave perf drop due to fragmentation + kernel path; mitigated by lower batch size, slightly higher timeout, lower max_new_tokens, per-layer-hybrid next. :thumbsup:

sara liu: adding checklist: 1) promote canary with new defaults 2) run per-layer quant sweep results due EOD 3) kernel profiling if sweep doesn't fully resolve 4) add rollout concurrency guard + quality gate

ci-bot: reminder: remember to update model-catalog entry with the new default values and the evaluation artifacts.
